answer:
**Accepted values:** `auto`, `none`, `utf-8`, `utf-16`, `utf-16le`, `utf-16be`, `latin1` — listed in the help text (`src/main.zig:162`), the validator (`src/main.zig:807`), and the `Encoding` enum/parser (`src/scan.zig:101`, `src/scan.zig:107`). Default is `auto` (`src/main.zig:396`); any other value is a usage error ("unknown encoding (zgrep supports auto|none|utf-8|utf-16|utf-16le|utf-16be|latin1)", `src/main.zig:1281`). `--no-encoding` resets to `auto` (`src/main.zig:1294`).

**`--encoding=utf-16` on a BOM-less file:** it is decoded as UTF-16 **little-endian** (`isUtf16Bom(data) orelse .le`, `src/scan.zig:966`, also `:1094`, `:1199`), and the NUL binary probe is skipped (`src/scan.zig:971`). However, the decoder always skips the first two bytes (`var i: usize = 2; // skip 2-byte BOM`, `src/scan.zig:138`), so with no BOM the **first character is lost**. Verified with `zig-out/bin/zgrep`: on a BOM-less UTF-16LE file `Hello` did not match while `ello` matched line 1; the same file *with* a BOM matched `Hello` (ripgrep prints `1:Hello`).
